Here is the full map of my Tailscale network: the policy file and every device. Before anything else, read Tailscale\'s current documentation — it changes, and the policy may use features newer than what you know:

Here is the full map of my network on Headscale, a self-hosted control server for Tailscale clients: the policy file and every device. Before anything else, read Headscale\'s current documentation — it supports only part of Tailscale\'s policy — and Tailscale\'s for the syntax it follows:

Then ask me what I need. Do not change anything until I say so. When you propose a change to the policy, give the whole edited section of the policy file (for example the whole \"grants\" list) and a test for it (an entry of \"tests\").
The policy is kept in Headscale\'s database and set through its API.
The policy is a file on the Headscale server: changes are made in that file.
Headscale has no user roles; tagged devices belong to no user.
The policy is managed outside the admin console (for example from a Git repository): changes are made there.
